comments.body:
Ah, it took me a while to figure out what the problem was. Just to clarify

So if I have a fedora instance whose repository root is at http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest
then do:
{{ curl -v -X POST -H "Content-Type: text/turtle" -d "<http://example.com/profile> a <test:whatever>." http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest
}}

I get back
{{
HTTP/1.1 400
Link: <http://localhost:8080/static/constraints/OutOfDomainSubjectException.rdf>; rel="http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#constrainedBy"
Content-Type: text/turtle
Content-Length: 97
Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2017 04:54:14 GMT
Connection: close

RDF Sream contains subject(s) (http://example.com/profile) not in the domain of this repository.
}}

The constrainedBy link results in a 404, since it does not point to a resource in Fedora's webapp context. It should be:
http://localhost:8080/*fcrepo/*static/constraints/OutOfDomainSubjectException.rdf
Aaron Birkland yes, the Link header in the response should be ".../fcrepo/static/constraints/..." – it is missing the "/fcrepo" portion

We have the UriInfo object, so extracting the correct context should be straight-forward:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-http-commons/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/http/commons/exceptionhandlers/ConstraintViolationExceptionMapper.java#L45

Kate Lynch, would you be interested in giving this bug a look?

I don't think it's as easy as grabbing the information from the UriInfo(), since it doesn't have the Servlet Context, which is what I think I'm looking for here - though I could be wrong. What I've done is this: 

        String path = uriInfo.getBaseUri().getPath(); 
        if (path.endsWith("/")) {
          path = path.substring(0, path.length() - 1);
        }

        LOGGER.warn("Path is: {}", path);
        final String constraintURI = uriInfo == null ? "" : String.format("%s://%s%s%s%s.rdf",
                uriInfo.getBaseUri().getScheme(), uriInfo.getBaseUri().getAuthority(),
                path, CONSTRAINT_DIR,
                e.getClass().toString().substring(e.getClass().toString().lastIndexOf('.') + 1));
        LOGGER.warn("Constructed Constraint URI: {}", constraintURI);
        return Link.fromUri(constraintURI).rel(CONSTRAINED_BY.getURI()).build();

This works in most cases, but is failing a test in the fcrepo-webapp module because the test tacks on a `/rest` to the original call, so the uriInfo.getBaseUri().getPath() seems to include that and then the test fails, since the rdf file is not located at that URI. (The test it fails is the fcrepo-webapp SanityCheckIT.java `testContraintLink()` and it tries to find the constraint file at: `http://localhost:51989/rest/static/constraints/ServerManagedPropertyException.rdf` )

I was thinking I need to grab the context of the Servlet since that would be reliable , but I'm really not sure how to do that in Java and in this framework - any pointers?

Bethany Seeger: You could potentially do something like this:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/compare/master...awoods:tmp
Andrew Woods - thank you, that's very helpful. I was starting to do something like this, but at the wrong level. I see now where to go. Thanks!

renderedFields.description:
When an ldp:constrainedBy link is included in an error response, the web app seems to expect that fedora is running in the root context of a servlet container:

For instance:

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Server: nginx/1.10.1
Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2017 20:32:57 GMT
Content-Type: text/turtle
Content-Length: 97
Connection: keep-alive
Link: <http://example.com/static/constraints/OutOfDomainSubjectException.rdf>; rel="http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#constrainedBy"

RDF Stream contains subject(s) (http://example.com/profile) not in the domain of this repository.

When in fact, Fedora is running in the /fcrepo context
